C0.quote: approval-based committee rule, R(A, k), is a social choice function
C0.note: Studies multi-winner approval voting rules applied before and after simulated deliberation.

C1.quote: We presented an empirical study of the relationship between deliberation
C1.note: All main results are simulations on synthetic Mallows-generated profiles that evaluate rules by welfare, representation and proportionality. The paper calls the study 'empirical', but it uses only synthetic data.

C2.1.value: approval profile; approval ballots; approval vote
C2.1.quote: takes as input an approval profile A and committee size k

C2.2.quote: has an approval ballot Ai ⊆ C, containing the set of its approved candidates
C2.2.note: Underlying rankings and cardinal utilities are held attitudes, not rule inputs.

C2.3.quote: we assume that agents have underlying cardinal utilities for candidates
C2.3.note: Agents also hold preference rankings Pi0.

C2.4.quote: The rankings are then converted to an approval ballot
C2.4.note: Ballots Ai, rankings Pi and utilities Ui are separate objects with separate notation. The ballot is derived from the ranking.

C3.1.quote: we assume agents are non-strategic and truthfully reveal their utilities

C3.2.quote: approval vote is then the set consisting of its bi top-ranked
C3.2.note: The vote is stated in words to be the top bi candidates of the agent's preference ranking. Footnote 3 also states that agents are non-strategic.

C3.3.quote: As is common in much of the deliberation literature
C3.3.note: The only reason given for non-strategic behaviour is a convention in prior work. This footnote concerns truthful reporting in deliberation; the statement on ballot formation gives no further reason.

C4.1.quote: cardinal utilities for candidates, consistent with their ordinal preferences
C4.1.note: Utilities are consistent with the ranking, and the approval set is the top bi candidates of that ranking.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: This ratio compares the (utilitarian) social welfare achieved by WR
C5.1.note: Utilitarian ratio, representation ratio, aggregate score and EJR/PJR satisfaction are evaluated in the simulations.

C5.2.quote: ui (c) ∈ R is the utility voter i derives from candidate c.
C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated on cardinal utilities that are separate from the ballots. Representation and EJR/PJR are evaluated on the approval inputs, which are derived from held rankings.

VOT.quote_behav: we assume agents are non-strategic and truthfully reveal their utilities
VOT.note: Voters act by speaking, by updating via a bounded confidence rule, and by voting; all of these actions are fixed by the model.

ORG.note: Group-formation strategies are experimental conditions; no organiser agent is modelled as choosing them.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: deliberation generally improves welfare and representation guarantees
This has ramifications on the practical use of such voting rules
This can serve to guide the design and deployment of voting

C9.2.quote: freezing agents' utilities once deliberation has concluded
C9.2.note: Needed and stated: the link between ballots and held utilities, and non-strategic voters. Needed but not stated: that post-deliberation utilities are the appropriate standard for comparing welfare before and after deliberation.
